readings.commitment: The United States was constituted by compact among sovereign states before 1787, and the Constitution must be read against that confederal baseline it replaced
readings.delta: Low central suppression (states retain sovereignty); beneficiary is state political classes; victim set is creditors and the union itself (no enforcement power); extractiveness minimal by incapacity

readings.commitment: The unamended 1787 text is a complete machine of enumerated powers whose structural design, not its later amendments, does the real constitutional work
readings.delta: Suppression by structure rather than rights (ambition counteracting ambition); beneficiary is the propertied founding coalition; victim set is the enslaved counted as three-fifths; extractiveness entrenched in the original compromises

readings.commitment: The Constitution's authority was perfected only by the 1791 rights amendments, which the ratifying public extracted as the price of union
readings.delta: Suppression redirected onto the federal government (negative liberties); beneficiary is the individual against federal power; victim set initially unchanged (no application to states); extractiveness checked at one level of government only

readings.commitment: The Constitution is a living amendment record whose operative meaning is set by successive waves of formal revision, above all Reconstruction, not by the founding text
readings.delta: Suppression of the original settlement by supersession; beneficiary expands with each wave (freedmen, women, eighteen-year-olds); victim set is defenders of each superseded order; extractiveness renegotiated era by era

readings.commitment: The Constitution is defined as much by the amendments the polity considered and refused as by those it ratified
readings.delta: Suppression by non-adoption (the refused alternative remains structurally absent); beneficiary is the status quo's beneficiaries; victim set is constituencies whose guarantees failed ratification; extractiveness preserved where change was refused

readings.commitment: The Articles of Confederation are a league of friendship among sovereign states, in which the central body is a congress of ambassadors with no power to tax or compel
readings.delta: Near-zero central suppression (unanimity for amendment, no execution power); beneficiary is state governments; victim set is continental creditors and interstate commerce; extractiveness nil by design and fatal in consequence

readings.commitment: The Northwest Ordinance is the confederation's enduring constitutional achievement, organizing territory into future equal states while banning slavery north of the Ohio
readings.delta: Suppression of colonial-style permanent dependency (statehood by formula); beneficiary is incoming settlers; victim set is the indigenous nations of the territory; extractiveness maximal toward the displaced, veiled by legal form

readings.commitment: The 1787 text's core is the separation of powers, in which liberty is protected by giving each branch the constitutional means and personal motives to resist the others
readings.delta: Suppression by mutual check (veto, advice-and-consent, impeachment); beneficiary is whoever benefits from government inaction; victim set is programs requiring sustained coordination; extractiveness limited by friction

readings.commitment: The 1787 text's core is federal supremacy, replacing the confederal league with a national government acting directly on individuals through supreme law
readings.delta: Suppression of state nullification (supremacy clause, federal judiciary); beneficiary is national commercial interests; victim set is state-level majorities overridden; extractiveness centralized and made collectible

readings.commitment: The 1787 text is structured by its slavery compromises, which purchased union by entrenching the slaveholding interest in representation, taxation, and fugitive rendition
readings.delta: Maximal suppression of the enslaved (codified as fractional persons); beneficiary is the slaveholding class with bonus representation; victim set is the enslaved and free Black persons subject to rendition; extractiveness total, constitutionally serviced

readings.commitment: The 1787 text's deepest commitment is Article V, which makes the Constitution alterable in principle but entrenches it in practice behind double supermajorities
readings.delta: Suppression of constitutional change itself (thirteen states can block); beneficiary is the settled order; victim set is durable supermajorities short of the threshold; extractiveness of the status quo compounds with time

readings.commitment: The Bill of Rights' first commitment is the First Amendment's protection of conscience and expression against federal establishment, prohibition, and censorship
readings.delta: Suppression of federal orthodoxy-making; beneficiary is dissenters, sects, and the press; victim set is officials who would police belief; extractiveness of conformity blocked at the federal level

readings.commitment: The Second and Third Amendments secure the people against the standing army the founders feared, through the militia and the inviolable home
readings.delta: Suppression of military domination of civil life; beneficiary is the armed citizenry and householders; victim set contested (whoever bears the cost of private arms); extractiveness of quartering and disarmament forbidden

readings.commitment: The Fourth through Eighth Amendments constitutionalize criminal procedure, interposing warrants, juries, counsel, and proportionality between the accused and the state
readings.delta: Suppression of inquisitorial shortcuts; beneficiary is the accused and the secure householder; victim set is prosecutors' efficiency; extractiveness of punishment bounded by process

readings.commitment: The Ninth and Tenth Amendments are the Bill of Rights' residuary clauses, reserving unenumerated rights to the people and undelegated powers to the states
readings.delta: Suppression of expansio-by-enumeration arguments; beneficiary is claimants of unlisted rights and state governments; victim set is federal power maximalists; extractiveness checked by the residuum

readings.commitment: The Establishment Clause forbids government endorsement or institutional entanglement with religion, keeping the state secular so that faith remains free
readings.delta: Suppression of official religion; beneficiary is religious minorities and the nonreligious; victim set is majorities seeking public religious affirmation; extractiveness of compelled support forbidden

readings.commitment: The Free Exercise Clause protects religious practice, not merely belief, against laws that burden the believer's obligations to conscience
readings.delta: Suppression of practice-burdening regulation; beneficiary is observant believers, especially minority faiths; victim set is uniform-application interests; extractiveness of forced violation of conscience forbidden

readings.commitment: The Free Speech Clause commits the polity to an open marketplace of expression in which government may not pick winners among viewpoints
readings.delta: Suppression of censorship itself; beneficiary is speakers, especially the despised; victim set is targets of protected harmful speech; extractiveness of orthodoxy enforcement forbidden

readings.commitment: The Free Press Clause protects the press as an institution, the only private business the Constitution names, because self-government requires an informed public
readings.delta: Suppression of prior restraint and licensing; beneficiary is publishers and their readers; victim set is officials whose conduct is exposed; extractiveness of information control forbidden

readings.commitment: The Assembly and Petition Clauses protect collective political action, the rights by which the otherwise powerless aggregate into a force government must hear
readings.delta: Suppression of anti-association measures; beneficiary is movements and the organized marginal; victim set is order-maintenance interests; extractiveness of enforced political atomization forbidden

readings.commitment: Establishment is measured by the Lemon test: a law must have secular purpose, a primary effect neither advancing nor inhibiting religion, and no excessive entanglement
readings.delta: Suppression via three-pronged scrutiny (broadest invalidation reach); beneficiary is separationist plaintiffs; victim set is accommodationist programs; extractiveness of public support for religion most tightly policed

readings.commitment: Establishment is measured by endorsement: whether a reasonable observer would perceive the government as sending a message that religion is favored and nonadherents are outsiders
readings.delta: Suppression keyed to social meaning rather than mechanics; beneficiary is the perceived-outsider observer; victim set is symbolic public religiosity; extractiveness of status subordination, not money, is the target

readings.commitment: Establishment requires coercion: government violates the clause only when it compels religious participation or support by force of law or social pressure
readings.delta: Narrowest suppression (only compulsion triggers); beneficiary is public religious expression; victim set is objectors who must show compulsion; extractiveness threshold raised to actual coercion

readings.commitment: Establishment is measured against historical practice: what the founding generation and unbroken tradition accepted cannot be an establishment now
readings.delta: Suppression anchored to founding-era baseline; beneficiary is longstanding practices (legislative prayer, monuments); victim set is novel claims against old forms; extractiveness grandfathered where traditional

readings.commitment: The Speech Clause's master rule is content neutrality: regulations targeting what is said get strict scrutiny, regulations of time, place, and manner get less
readings.delta: Suppression of viewpoint-targeting laws; beneficiary is disfavored viewpoints; victim set is governments with content-based aims; extractiveness of selective silencing strictly policed

readings.commitment: The Speech Clause operates through historic categories: incitement, obscenity, defamation, true threats, and fighting words fall outside protection by definition
readings.delta: Suppression confined to enumerated categories; beneficiary is speakers outside the categories; victim set is harms that fit no category; extractiveness of new exceptions resisted

readings.commitment: The Speech Clause's geography is the forum doctrine: streets and parks held in trust for expression, with government's regulatory power scaling by forum type
readings.delta: Suppression varies by property class; beneficiary is speakers in traditional forums; victim set is speakers in nonpublic forums; extractiveness of access fees and permits forum-graded

readings.commitment: Free exercise yields to neutral laws of general applicability: religion gets no exemption from rules that do not target it
readings.delta: Low suppression of regulation (rational basis for neutral laws); beneficiary is uniform regulatory schemes; victim set is minority practices burdened incidentally; extractiveness of incidental burdens permitted

readings.commitment: Free exercise requires accommodation: any substantial burden on religious practice demands a compelling state interest pursued by the least restrictive means
readings.delta: High suppression of burdening regulation (strict scrutiny); beneficiary is burdened believers; victim set is regulatory uniformity; extractiveness of forced compliance strictly limited

readings.commitment: The Second Amendment secures the right to keep and bear arms, the provision whose prefatory militia clause and operative right have divided interpreters for two centuries
readings.delta: Suppression of disarmament measures (scope contested); beneficiary is arms-bearers; victim set is contested (regulation interests or the disarmed); extractiveness of confiscation forbidden within the right's scope

readings.commitment: The Third Amendment forbids peacetime quartering of soldiers in private homes, the founders' direct answer to a specific imperial abuse
readings.delta: Suppression of military imposition on the household; beneficiary is householders; victim set is military logistics convenience; extractiveness of forced quartering forbidden

readings.commitment: The Second Amendment protects a collective right tied to militia service: the people keep and bear arms as members of the organized state militia, not as private individuals
readings.delta: Suppression of federal disarmament of state militias only; beneficiary is state military institutions; victim set is individual-right claimants; extractiveness of private arms regulation unconstrained

readings.commitment: The Second Amendment protects an individual right to keep and bear arms for self-defense, with the militia clause announcing a purpose, not a limitation
readings.delta: Suppression of broad gun regulation (Heller scrutiny); beneficiary is individual gun owners; victim set is comprehensive-regulation jurisdictions; extractiveness of disarmament forbidden at the individual level

readings.commitment: The Fourth Amendment secures persons, houses, papers, and effects against unreasonable searches and seizures, conditioning intrusion on warrants and probable cause
readings.delta: Suppression of general warrants and dragnets; beneficiary is the surveilled and searched; victim set is investigative efficiency; extractiveness of evidence bounded by reasonableness

readings.commitment: The Fifth Amendment bundles the grand jury, double jeopardy, self-incrimination, due process, and takings guarantees into a single charter against state overreach
readings.delta: Suppression of compelled self-conviction and uncompensated taking; beneficiary is the accused and the property-holder; victim set is prosecutorial and eminent-domain convenience; extractiveness conditioned on process and compensation

readings.commitment: The Sixth Amendment guarantees the machinery of fair trial: speed, publicity, jury, confrontation, compulsory process, and counsel
readings.delta: Suppression of secret and counsel-less prosecution; beneficiary is criminal defendants; victim set is summary-justice interests; extractiveness of conviction routed through adversarial testing

readings.commitment: The Seventh Amendment preserves the civil jury, entrenching lay fact-finding in private disputes against judicial consolidation
readings.delta: Suppression of bench-only civil adjudication; beneficiary is civil litigants preferring lay judgment; victim set is judicial economy; extractiveness of judge-controlled outcomes checked by the jury

readings.commitment: The Eighth Amendment forbids excessive bail, excessive fines, and cruel and unusual punishments, importing proportionality into the penal power
readings.delta: Suppression of punitive excess; beneficiary is the convicted and detained; victim set is maximal-deterrence policy; extractiveness of punishment bounded by proportion

readings.commitment: The Fourth Amendment's two clauses are linked: searches are presumptively unreasonable without a warrant, and exceptions must stay jealously confined
readings.delta: High suppression of warrantless search (exceptions enumerated and narrow); beneficiary is the searched; victim set is exigency-claiming officers; extractiveness of evidence routed through the magistrate

readings.commitment: The Fourth Amendment's touchstone is reasonableness standing alone: the warrant clause governs warrants when used, but the ultimate test is a balance of interests
readings.delta: Lower suppression (balancing admits more intrusions); beneficiary is special-needs and administrative search regimes; victim set is warrant-preference formalists; extractiveness of evidence weighed case by case

readings.commitment: The Fifth Amendment's core is the privilege against self-incrimination, forbidding the state to make the accused the instrument of his own conviction
readings.delta: Suppression of compelled testimony (Miranda prophylaxis); beneficiary is suspects under interrogation; victim set is confession-dependent prosecution; extractiveness of coerced statements excluded

readings.commitment: The Fifth Amendment's core is the double jeopardy bar, giving verdicts finality so the state cannot retry the acquitted into exhaustion
readings.delta: Suppression of serial reprosecution; beneficiary is the acquitted; victim set is prosecution second chances; extractiveness of repeated process forbidden

readings.commitment: The Fifth Amendment's takings clause permits eminent domain but prices it, requiring just compensation whenever private property is taken for public use
readings.delta: Suppression of uncompensated expropriation; beneficiary is property-holders in the state's path; victim set is costless-acquisition government; extractiveness converted to a compensated transaction

readings.commitment: Cruel and unusual means what it meant in 1791: punishments are forbidden only if they were cruel by founding-era standards or add terror to traditional methods
readings.delta: Suppression frozen at the founding baseline; beneficiary is traditional punishment regimes; victim set is evolving-decency claimants; extractiveness of historical punishments preserved

readings.commitment: Cruel and unusual draws meaning from the evolving standards of decency that mark the progress of a maturing society
readings.delta: Suppression expands with social consensus (death penalty narrowing); beneficiary is categories newly protected (juveniles, the intellectually disabled); victim set is retributive maximalism; extractiveness of punishment ratchets downward

readings.commitment: The Ninth Amendment declares that enumerating rights shall not be construed to deny others retained by the people, the textual home of unenumerated rights
readings.delta: Suppression of enumeration-as-exhaustion arguments; beneficiary is claimants of unlisted liberties; victim set is strict-enumeration interpreters; extractiveness checked beyond the listed rights

readings.commitment: The Tenth Amendment reserves undelegated powers to the states and the people, the structural anchor of constitutional federalism
readings.delta: Suppression of federal commandeering; beneficiary is state governments; victim set is national uniform schemes; extractiveness of state machinery by federal mandate forbidden

readings.commitment: The Reconstruction Amendments are a second founding, abolishing slavery, nationalizing citizenship and rights, and enfranchising the freedmen by constitutional command
readings.delta: Suppression of the slaveholding order and state rights-abridgment; beneficiary is the freedmen and later all rights-claimants against states; victim set is the defeated Confederate settlement; extractiveness of bondage abolished, of subordination contested

readings.commitment: The Progressive era amendments retooled the constitutional machine: income taxation, direct election of senators, prohibition, and woman suffrage within seven years
readings.delta: Suppression of Gilded Age intermediaries (legislature-chosen senators, untaxed accumulation); beneficiary is national reform majorities and women voters; victim set is the saloon and the state-legislature broker; extractiveness nationalized through the income tax

readings.commitment: The mid-century amendments extended the franchise's reach: presidential votes for the capital, abolition of the poll tax, presidential succession, and the eighteen-year-old vote
readings.delta: Suppression of franchise gatekeeping devices; beneficiary is poor voters, D.C. residents, and the young; victim set is restrictionist state regimes; extractiveness of the poll tax abolished

readings.commitment: A quieter family of amendments maintains the machine itself: electoral mechanics, terms and sessions, repeal of prohibition, term limits, and congressional pay
readings.delta: Suppression of identified mechanical failures (contingent elections, lame ducks, third terms); beneficiary is institutional regularity; victim set is incumbents advantaged by the old mechanics; extractiveness of self-dealing pay raises delayed

readings.commitment: The Thirteenth Amendment abolishes slavery and involuntary servitude everywhere in the United States, the only amendment that binds private actors directly
readings.delta: Suppression of chattel bondage including private; beneficiary is the formerly enslaved; victim set is the slaveholding economy; extractiveness of forced labor abolished, save the punishment clause

readings.commitment: The Fourteenth Amendment nationalizes citizenship and forbids states to abridge privileges or immunities, deny due process, or deny equal protection
readings.delta: Suppression of state-level subordination; beneficiary is citizens against their own states; victim set is state autonomy over civil status; extractiveness of caste by state law forbidden

readings.commitment: The Fifteenth Amendment forbids denying the vote on account of race, color, or previous condition of servitude
readings.delta: Suppression of explicit racial disfranchisement; beneficiary is Black male voters; victim set is white-supremacist electoral regimes; extractiveness of representation without the franchise forbidden in terms

readings.commitment: The Thirteenth Amendment abolished the legal institution of slavery and nothing more: it ended the property relation, not its social aftermath
readings.delta: Suppression confined to the formal institution; beneficiary is the legally freed; victim set is claims against slavery's incidents; extractiveness of the punishment-clause exception preserved

readings.commitment: The Thirteenth Amendment empowers Congress to eradicate the badges and incidents of slavery, reaching private discrimination that perpetuates the abolished system
readings.delta: Suppression extends to slavery's residue (private discrimination reachable); beneficiary is victims of race-based exclusion; victim set is private discriminators; extractiveness of caste-maintenance practices reachable by statute

readings.commitment: The Citizenship Clause makes everyone born or naturalized in the United States a citizen, overruling Dred Scott and placing membership beyond political revocation
readings.delta: Suppression of citizenship-stripping and birthright denial; beneficiary is the native-born regardless of ancestry; victim set is nativist membership gatekeeping; extractiveness of statelessness forbidden at birth

readings.commitment: The Fourteenth Amendment's Due Process Clause forbids states to deprive any person of life, liberty, or property without due process of law, the vehicle of incorporation and substantive liberty
readings.delta: Suppression of arbitrary state deprivation; beneficiary is rights-holders against states; victim set is unreviewable state process; extractiveness of liberty and property conditioned on process

readings.commitment: The Equal Protection Clause forbids states to deny any person the equal protection of the laws, the Constitution's general guarantee against caste
readings.delta: Suppression of state-imposed hierarchy; beneficiary is disfavored classes; victim set is classification-dependent regimes; extractiveness of subordinating classification forbidden

readings.commitment: The Privileges or Immunities Clause was meant to be the Fourteenth Amendment's engine, protecting the substantive rights of national citizenship until the Slaughter-House Cases hollowed it
readings.delta: Suppression intended against state abridgment of national rights, judicially stunted; beneficiary was to be all citizens, in practice few; victim set is the clause's intended scope; extractiveness analysis displaced into due process

readings.commitment: Due process means process: notice, hearing, and a neutral decision-maker before the state takes liberty or property, with the process due scaling by the stakes
readings.delta: Suppression of summary deprivation; beneficiary is benefit-holders and the accused; victim set is administrative speed; extractiveness conditioned on Mathews balancing

readings.commitment: Due process has substance: some liberties are so fundamental that no process suffices to take them, from parental control to marriage and bodily autonomy
readings.delta: Suppression of rights-invading legislation regardless of procedure; beneficiary is holders of unenumerated fundamental liberties; victim set is majoritarian moral regulation; extractiveness of fundamental liberty strictly scrutinized

readings.commitment: Due process is the conduit through which the Bill of Rights binds the states, incorporating the enumerated guarantees one by one against state governments
readings.delta: Suppression of state exemption from the Bill of Rights; beneficiary is rights-holders against states; victim set is state criminal-procedure autonomy; extractiveness checked at both levels of government

readings.commitment: Classifications by race or burdening fundamental rights are presumptively unconstitutional, surviving only if narrowly tailored to a compelling interest
readings.delta: Maximal suppression of suspect classification (strict in theory, fatal in fact); beneficiary is racial minorities against hostile classification; victim set is race-conscious programs of any valence; extractiveness of racial sorting near-categorically forbidden

readings.commitment: Sex-based classifications get intermediate scrutiny: they must serve important objectives by substantially related means, with an exceedingly persuasive justification
readings.delta: Substantial suppression of sex classification short of the racial standard; beneficiary is sex-discrimination plaintiffs; victim set is real-differences rationales; extractiveness of sex-role enforcement substantially limited

readings.commitment: Ordinary economic and social classifications need only a rational relation to a legitimate purpose, a tier of near-total deference to legislative line-drawing
readings.delta: Minimal suppression (almost everything survives); beneficiary is legislative classification freedom; victim set is non-suspect-class claimants; extractiveness of ordinary regulatory burden unreviewed in practice

readings.commitment: The Fifteenth Amendment forbids only explicit racial conditions on voting: facially neutral devices like literacy tests and poll taxes stand outside its terms
readings.delta: Suppression confined to facial racial bars; beneficiary is states deploying neutral devices; victim set is voters disfranchised by proxy; extractiveness of the franchise continued by indirection

readings.commitment: The Fifteenth Amendment reaches any device that operates to deny the vote by race, empowering Congress to dismantle disfranchisement by results, as the Voting Rights Act did
readings.delta: Suppression of disfranchisement in operation, not just in terms; beneficiary is minority voters under federal protection; victim set is vote-dilution and gatekeeping regimes; extractiveness of representation policed by effect

readings.commitment: The Sixteenth Amendment authorizes the federal income tax without apportionment, the fiscal foundation of the modern national state
readings.delta: Suppression of the apportionment shield around accumulated wealth; beneficiary is the national treasury and redistribution; victim set is high incomes previously beyond reach; extractiveness nationalized and progressive by design

readings.commitment: The Seventeenth Amendment takes Senate elections from state legislatures and gives them to the people, ending the era of the bought legislature and the brokered seat
readings.delta: Suppression of legislature-mediated selection; beneficiary is statewide electorates; victim set is state party machines and the federalism the old method anchored; extractiveness of the purchased Senate seat abolished

readings.commitment: The Eighteenth Amendment wrote prohibition into the Constitution itself, the one attempt to use fundamental law for direct social regulation, repealed within fourteen years
readings.delta: Maximal suppression of the liquor trade by constitutional command; beneficiary is the temperance coalition; victim set is drinkers, brewers, and the rule of law under bootlegging; extractiveness displaced into the criminal market

readings.commitment: The Nineteenth Amendment forbids denying the vote on account of sex, ending the world's longest suffrage campaign with fourteen words
readings.delta: Suppression of sex-based disfranchisement; beneficiary is women voters; victim set is the male-only electorate's gatekeepers; extractiveness of representation without the franchise ended in terms

readings.commitment: The Nineteenth Amendment did exactly what it says: it enfranchised women and left every other legal disability of sex untouched
readings.delta: Suppression confined to ballot denial; beneficiary is women as voters only; victim set is claims of broader sex equality grounded in the amendment; extractiveness of coverture's residue unaddressed

readings.commitment: The Nineteenth Amendment stands for women's full and equal citizenship, a structural commitment that should inform sex-equality interpretation across the Constitution
readings.delta: Suppression of sex hierarchy read structurally from the franchise; beneficiary is sex-equality jurisprudence; victim set is suffrage-only minimalism; extractiveness of subordination read as constitutionally disfavored

readings.commitment: The Twenty-Third Amendment gives the District of Columbia electoral votes for president, partial recognition for a capital population larger than some states
readings.delta: Suppression of total capital disfranchisement; beneficiary is D.C. residents in presidential elections only; victim set is full-representation claims (no Congress seats); extractiveness of taxation without representation reduced, not ended

readings.commitment: The Twenty-Fourth Amendment abolishes the poll tax in federal elections, severing the franchise from the ability to pay
readings.delta: Suppression of wealth-conditioned voting; beneficiary is poor voters of every race; victim set is fiscal gatekeeping regimes; extractiveness of paying to vote forbidden federally

readings.commitment: The Twenty-Fifth Amendment regularizes presidential disability and succession, providing the machinery for an incapacitated executive the founders never specified
readings.delta: Suppression of succession ambiguity; beneficiary is continuity of the executive; victim set is contested-incapacity maneuvering; extractiveness of power seized through ambiguity foreclosed

readings.commitment: The Twenty-Sixth Amendment lowers the voting age to eighteen, ratified in record time on the principle that those old enough to be drafted are old enough to vote
readings.delta: Suppression of age-based disfranchisement above eighteen; beneficiary is young voters; victim set is age-restrictionist states; extractiveness of conscription without the franchise ended

readings.commitment: The Twelfth Amendment separates electoral votes for president and vice president, repairing the original design after the deadlock of 1800
readings.delta: Suppression of the tie-by-design failure mode; beneficiary is party-ticket coherence; victim set is the runner-up vice presidency; extractiveness of office through electoral accident foreclosed

readings.commitment: The Twentieth Amendment moves inauguration to January and kills the lame-duck congressional session that governed after losing
readings.delta: Suppression of repudiated-majority lawmaking; beneficiary is incoming electoral verdicts; victim set is defeated incumbents' final leverage; extractiveness of post-defeat dealmaking curtailed

readings.commitment: The Twenty-First Amendment repeals prohibition, the only amendment to repeal another, and returns liquor control to the states
readings.delta: Suppression of the failed national experiment; beneficiary is the legal liquor trade and state regulators; victim set is the temperance settlement; extractiveness rechanneled from bootleggers to licensed markets

readings.commitment: The Twenty-Second Amendment limits presidents to two terms, constitutionalizing the Washington tradition that Roosevelt broke
readings.delta: Suppression of executive perpetuation; beneficiary is rotation in office; victim set is popular incumbents and their coalitions; extractiveness of accumulated incumbency power capped

readings.commitment: The Twenty-Seventh Amendment delays congressional pay raises until after an election, ratified 203 years after Madison proposed it
readings.delta: Suppression of self-dealing compensation; beneficiary is electoral accountability over pay; victim set is sitting members' immediate raises; extractiveness of self-voted pay deferred past a verdict

readings.commitment: The Equal Rights Amendment would have made equality of rights regardless of sex an explicit constitutional command, passed by Congress in 1972 and never validly ratified
readings.delta: Suppression of sex classification by express text, refused; beneficiary would have been sex-equality claimants with a textual anchor; victim set under refusal is claims left to intermediate scrutiny; extractiveness of sex hierarchy left to doctrine rather than text

readings.commitment: The Child Labor Amendment would have empowered Congress to regulate the labor of persons under eighteen, stalled in the states until the New Deal mooted it
readings.delta: Suppression of child labor by constitutional grant, refused then mooted; beneficiary would have been working children; victim set under refusal was federal power until commerce doctrine shifted; extractiveness of child labor ended by statute instead

readings.commitment: The D.C. Voting Rights Amendment would have given the capital full congressional representation, passed in 1978 and dead at sixteen ratifications
readings.delta: Suppression of capital disfranchisement, refused; beneficiary would have been D.C. residents as full constituents; victim set under refusal is the unrepresented capital; extractiveness of federal taxation without House or Senate voice continues

readings.commitment: The Balanced Budget Amendment would constitutionalize fiscal balance, repeatedly passed by one chamber and never sent to the states
readings.delta: Suppression of deficit finance by fundamental law, refused; beneficiary would be future taxpayers against present borrowing; victim set under adoption would be countercyclical policy; extractiveness across generations left to politics

readings.commitment: The ERA commands sex-blindness: law may not classify by sex at all, making sex what race is under strict scrutiny
readings.delta: Maximal suppression of sex classification of any valence; beneficiary is formal-equality claimants; victim set is sex-conscious protective and remedial law; extractiveness of all sex-based sorting forbidden

readings.commitment: The ERA targets subordination, not classification: it forbids law that perpetuates women's inferior status while permitting measures that dismantle hierarchy
readings.delta: Suppression keyed to hierarchy rather than classification; beneficiary is substantive-equality claimants; victim set is subordinating practices however facially neutral; extractiveness of sex hierarchy the direct target
